---
title: "Build a clock"
subtitle: "Compare learners on your own data, choose one on an honest error, and fit it"
---

When no published clock fits your assay or your question, fit one to your cohort. FALCONAge
compares several learners first, every number out of fold, and then fits the one you choose.

## 1. Compare learners

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Python

```python
import falconage as fa

d   = fa.prepare(fa.read_betas("betas.csv"))      # obs must hold the target, e.g. "age"
cmp = fa.compare_learners(d, target="age", groups="person")

cmp.table          # one row per learner: MAE, MedAE, r, slope, bias by thirds, seconds
cmp.selected       # the nested error of "pick the best": the number to report
cmp.best           # the learner with the lowest out-of-fold MAE
```

### R

```r
library(FALCONAge)

d   <- prepare(read_betas("betas.csv"))
cmp <- compare_learners(d, target = "age", groups = "person")

cmp$table
cmp$selected
```

:::

`groups` names a sample-sheet column whose members always stay on the same side of a split:
the person, when there are repeated visits, or the batch or cohort, for leave-one-group-out.
Without it, a person's second visit is predicted by a model that was trained on their first.

## 2. The learners

| Name | What it is | Writes a clock file | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `elasticnet` | glmnet's elastic net, alpha 0.5, lambda by inner cross-validation | yes | nothing extra |
| `lasso`, `ridge` | the same with alpha 1 and 0 | yes | nothing extra |
| `screened_elasticnet` | the 2,000 CpGs most correlated with the target, then elastic net; the screen runs inside each training part | yes | nothing extra |
| `pc_elasticnet` | principal components, then elastic net; maps back to one weight per CpG | yes | nothing extra |
| `random_forest`, `gradient_boosting`, `svr`, `mlp` | scikit-learn regressors | no | `pip install "falconage[learn]"` (in the Docker image already) |

Pass `transform="horvath"` to fit Horvath's log-linear transform of age and invert it, which
matters when the cohort includes children.

## 3. Read the comparison honestly

- **Quote `selected`, not the best row of `table`.** Picking the best of several learners is
  itself a fitted choice, so the winner's own error is optimistic. `selected` repeats the pick
  inside each outer fold and measures it on samples the pick never saw.
- **Look at the slope and the bias by thirds**, not only MAE. Every penalised model pulls
  predictions towards the mean, so the old read young and the young read old.
- **The most accurate age predictor is not necessarily the best biomarker.** Test the residual
  against an outcome on a cohort the model was not fitted on.

## 4. Fit the chosen learner and save it

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Python

```python
fit = fa.fit_clock(d, target="age", learner="pc_elasticnet", groups="person")
fit.metrics                        # out-of-fold MAE, MedAE, r, slope
fit.to_clock("mycohortclock", "my_clocks/")
```

### R

```r
fit <- fit_clock(d, target = "age", learner = "pc_elasticnet", groups = "person")
fit$metrics
clock_to_file(fit, "mycohortclock", "my_clocks/")
```

:::

`to_clock` writes `mycohortclock.yaml`, its coefficients and its reference values into
`my_clocks/`. [Add a clock](add.qmd) scores it like any catalogue clock.

→ **Why it works this way:** [Building a clock](../methods/building.qmd)
